parts.note: a vinyl disc is turned over to play its second face, so the clue describes that other face of a record

explanation.surface: A query about flipping a gramophone disc, dressed up like a sales figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn-over' looks like business jargon for sales; here it is the physical act of turning a record over.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-side of a single is the face you hear only after turning the disc over.

clue.text: Sloppy lines written in extremes of fancy

indicators.note: written in says one piece is set down inside the other
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from fancy

parts.note: rows are lines, as of seats or text

explanation.surface: Careless lines of verse written in an ornate style.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsy describes someone scruffy and unkempt, a synonym for slovenly in appearance.

clue.text: React in an odd way, unaware of what's going on

indicators.note: doing something in an odd way means the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone behaving strangely because they are oblivious to their surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in an' belongs to the fodder: the letters of REACT IN AN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dazed or hypnotised is oblivious to the events around them.

parts.note: play here is a theatrical script, and its rules are the printed instructions telling actors where to move

explanation.surface: A question about the regulations of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests a game with rules; it is a drama, whose script tells the actors what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripts carry instructions to performers such as exits and entrances, guiding how a drama is staged.

clue.text: Refuse to recite all the cases

definitions.meaning: to refuse is to turn down an offer
in Latin grammar, to list a noun's forms in nominative, accusative and so on is to inflect it through every case

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to go through every legal case they have handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests law; it means grammatical cases, as schoolchildren recite Latin nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning down an invitation and listing a noun's inflected forms share one verb.

clue.text: Prophet is first-class, given a head start

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first-class, written here with the letter I standing for the figure one

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of head

explanation.surface: A prophet who is excellent and also gets an early lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI; 'head start' splits into the start of 'head', giving H.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the major Old Testament prophets.

clue.text: Standard wear for officers and NCOs

definitions.text: Standard wear for officers and NCOs

parts.words: Standard wear for officers and NCOs
parts.note: a standard is a flag, and its emblems are the insignia that officers and non-commissioned officers wear on their uniforms

explanation.surface: A remark on regulation uniform for military ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning regular; it is a flag. Officers wear stars as rank insignia and NCOs (non-commissioned officers such as sergeants) wear chevrons.
explanation.definitionFit: The US flag shows white emblems on blue and red and white bands, the same symbols as military rank badges.

parts.note: Bury is an English football club, and the clue asks what plays that role in Milan, while bury also means to put in a grave

explanation.surface: A question about funerals in the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town and football club in Lancashire; its Milanese counterpart is the club Internazionale, whose short name is also the verb meaning bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb a body is the verb, and it is also the short name of a famous Milan football club.

clue.text: A bloomer, taking part in such a rebellion

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone making a blunder while joining an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell-like wild flower is a plant that blossoms, so it is a bloomer.

indicators.note: after says the tear piece follows the father piece

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a rent is a tear, as in fabric

explanation.surface: A rip in the clothing of one's dad or mum.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an &lit: the whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, since a father or mother is exactly what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Either a father or a mother is one who has a child.

clue.text: Tomahawk held by American Indian? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: held by, turned round by quite the opposite, means the native people is contained in the weapon word

explanation.surface: A Native American warrior carrying a hatchet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' reverses the surface: not the tomahawk held by the Indian, but the Indian held inside 'Tomahawk'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Omaha are a Native American people of Nebraska.

definitions.meaning: a type is a kind of person, as in an odd sort
any single written symbol of an alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to key in a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of a certain sort and a single written symbol share one noun.

clue.text: Work for the enemy, as a prisoner might do

parts.note: to serve is to work for someone
time is called the enemy, from the old saying

explanation.surface: Collaborating with the foe, the way a captive might.
explanation.walkthrough: Time as 'the enemy' is a crossword convention from the saying that time is the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict spends a sentence in jail, which is the idiom for this phrase.

indicators.note: straggling suggests something spread untidily, so the letters of the word curbs are scattered

explanation.surface: Restraints on overgrown shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is low stunted vegetation such as brushwood.

definitions.meaning: after a while, sooner or later
arriving at the agreed hour, not late

explanation.surface: Someone who finally turns up on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'sooner or later' and 'not late', two senses of one idiom.

clue.text: Melodic way of having fun with a lute

indicators.note: a way of having the letters is a rearrangement of them, here of fun and lute together

explanation.surface: A tuneful method of enjoying oneself with a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodious is pleasant to hear and full of tunes.

parts.note: light meals sound like snacks, but taken literally they are flames swallowed by a circus performer

explanation.surface: A question about someone who prefers snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like 'not heavy'; it means burning, a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus act who swallows flames could be said to dine on light.

clue.text: Hero achieves eminence amongst top men

indicators.note: amongst says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: aces are top performers, the best
an eminence is a hill, a raised piece of ground

explanation.surface: A hero rises to prominence among the leading figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' looks like fame; it is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek warrior of Homer's Iliad.

parts.note: fair weather is mild, and the name of that mildness is also the name of an early pope and saint

explanation.surface: A query about a patron saint of good weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild weather is described with this adjective, and St Clement was an early bishop of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild weather has this adjective, which is also the name of a saint.

parts.note: office keys suggest door keys, but the keys meant are those of a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone unlocking the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' suggests locks; it means a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing keys on a keyboard to produce text is the office task meant.

parts.note: saving face usually means avoiding embarrassment, but literally it is protecting the face, as a knight's helmet did

explanation.surface: Old methods of avoiding humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving face' is an idiom for keeping dignity; here it is literal protection of the face by a helmet's movable front.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's helmet had a hinged front piece shielding the face in battle.

clue.text: Providentially, pointer is removed, possibly with legal force

indicators.note: is removed says the letters of the word pointer are taken away from the longer word
possibly says the letters that remain are then rearranged

explanation.surface: Through good fortune, a dog is taken away, perhaps lawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of POINTER from PROVIDENTIALLY, leaving VDIALLY, which 'possibly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done lawfully, in a binding way, is done in a manner the law upholds.

clue.text: They may have fallen on people's feet

definitions.text: They may have fallen on people's feet

parts.words: They may have fallen on people's feet
parts.note: fallen suggests things dropped onto feet, but it describes the curved parts of the foot that have flattened

explanation.surface: Objects that might have dropped onto someone's toes.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat feet are said to have fallen arches: the curves of the sole have collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved parts of a foot's sole can flatten, a condition called fallen.

clue.text: It has a small part in a big picture

definitions.text: It has a small part in a big picture

parts.words: It has a small part in a big picture
parts.note: a small part in a big picture sounds like a bit-part actor in a film, but it is a small image set within a larger one

explanation.surface: An extra with a minor role in an epic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part in a big picture' suggests a film role; it is a small map or picture set inside a larger one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small diagram placed within a larger illustration or map is this.

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the letters of arson are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A fire-raiser destroys a piece of navigation equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships detect objects under water by sending sound pulses and timing the echoes.

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: sort of says the letters of arboreal are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling creature that keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arboreal' looks like a description of the animal; its letters become OLARBEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This white Arctic mammal is a large carnivore.

parts.note: a state can be a country, and a nodding sleepy person is said to be in this imaginary country of sleep

explanation.surface: A question about a drowsy condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' means a nation as well as a condition; the biblical land east of Eden doubles as a name for sleep, since nodding off is a sign of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for sleep, playing on the biblical place and nodding off.

definitions.meaning: as in ...-black, a tarry black substance
a street vendor's regular spot or stall site

explanation.surface: Where an illicit dealer operates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black market' reads as one phrase; it splits after 'Black'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar-like dark resin and a vendor's allotted spot share one word.

definitions.meaning: in engineering, a load or pressure acting on a body
special weight placed on a syllable or point

explanation.surface: A statement about the power of putting weight on words.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical pressure on a material and weight laid on a syllable share one noun.

clue.text: They are irritating for sightseers, naturally

definitions.text: They are irritating for sightseers, naturally

parts.words: They are irritating for sightseers, naturally
parts.note: sightseers here are those who see, and painful red eyes literally irritate them, while ugly sights figuratively irritate tourists

explanation.surface: A complaint about blots on the landscape that annoy tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: Ugly buildings irritate tourists; read literally, sore eyes are the irritation of those who see.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly things that offend the eye are the idiom, and literally they are painful eyes.
